entries.what_happened: Four manuscripts, all stated over Q̄. (1) 'The abelian Zilber–Pink conjecture' claims that for every abelian variety A over a number field K and every irreducible subvariety X ⊆ A over Q̄, X has only finitely many maximal atypical subvarieties. Atypicality is measured in S = ⟨X⟩_sp, the smallest torsion coset containing X: an irreducible Y is atypical if it is a component of X ∩ T for a torsion coset T ⊆ S with dim Y > dim X + dim T − dim S. The text also gives an equivalent form: finitely many proper atypical Y₁,…,Y_m such that every atypical subvariety lies in one of them. The route is a non-density theorem (if X lies in no proper torsion coset, X ∩ A^[dim X+1] is not Zariski dense in X, where A^[r] is the union of torsion cosets of codimension ≥ r), proved via an auxiliary sequence theorem (§§2–8), and then a reduction to maximal-atypical finiteness using Barroero–Dill Thm 1.9 and Habegger–Pila Thm 9.8 (§9). A finite-rank translated-intersection corollary is also stated. (2) 'The E×CM component of Zilber–Pink for curves in A₂' claims that a reduced irreducible Hodge-generic curve C ⊂ A₂ over Q̄ has only finitely many points s whose abelian surface is isogenous to E₁×E₂ with at least one factor CM (isogenies need not respect the polarization; the both-CM case is included). Its new input is a Galois-orbit lower bound for 'mixed' points (one CM, one non-CM factor): orbit size ≥ c·max{N(s), |disc End(F)|}^(1/42), where N(s) is the minimal degree of a product isogeny; the constant depends on C and K and is ineffective. Finiteness then follows from Daw–Orr's implication (their Thm 1.2, as corrected) and, for the both-CM and special points, Andre–Oort for A₂ (Pila–Tsimerman). (3) 'Quaternionic division points on curves in the Siegel threefold' claims that a reduced irreducible Hodge-generic closed curve C ⊂ A₂ over Q̄ has only finitely many points whose full geometric endomorphism algebra is an indefinite quaternion division algebra over ℚ. It proves a height bound h(t) ≤ c[K(t):K]^c′ for such points (Thm thm:height), via a common-relation interpolation theorem (§2) and Frobenius cross-pairings in a rank-five quadratic variation, then a counting argument: the period image would lie in a subset of the isotropic quadric of dimension ≤ 2, whereas full monodromy makes it Zariski dense. (4) 'Elliptic squares and Zilber–Pink for curves in A₂' claims that a Hodge-generic curve C ⊂ A₂ over Q̄ has only finitely many points whose abelian surface is isogenous to E² with E non-CM. It proves a Galois-orbit bound for these points in terms of the discriminant of the full endomorphism order and applies Daw–Orr's conditional counting theorem in its E² case, the orbit bound supplying its hypothesis. It then states the full curve case: for Hodge-generic C over Q̄, only finitely many points of C lie on special subvarieties of dimension ≤ 1 (this combines (4) with the companion theorems (2) and (3)), plus a special-closure corollary for every curve over Q̄.
entries.delivers: Does not settle the frozen problem, which is stated over C and covers mixed Shimura and semiabelian varieties in general. What is claimed, all over Q̄ only: (a) Abelian varieties (ambient class (2), abelian case): for every abelian variety over Q̄ and every irreducible subvariety, finitely many maximal atypical subvarieties, with atypicality relative to the smallest containing torsion coset. That is the 'maximal' reading. The literal frozen reading ('finitely many atypical subvarieties') is not what is proved: the manuscript gives finitely many maximal ones and says every atypical subvariety lies in one of them, but makes no finiteness claim for the set of all atypical subvarieties. (b) A₂ (a pure Shimura variety, ambient class (1)), curves only: for Hodge-generic curves over Q̄, finitely many points on special subvarieties of dimension ≤ 1, which is the full curve case (Thm intro:zp in (4)). For a Hodge-generic curve in A₂ the atypical subvarieties are points (a special surface meets it only in points, which are not atypical there), so the 'all' and 'maximal' readings coincide in that case. That is my reading of the definition, not a statement in the manuscripts. For non-Hodge-generic curves over Q̄, the special-closure corollary gives the analogous finiteness, with codimension taken inside the smallest special S_C containing the curve. (c) Quantifier (3): all subvarieties of abelian varieties over Q̄; only curves in A₂. (d) Atypicality convention: the manuscripts take codimension inside the smallest special subvariety containing X. The frozen list does not say which ambient S it means, so the judge should check that choice. The manuscripts do not claim to resolve the conjecture as stated.
entries.remains: If the claims are correct, still open: (a) the statement over C, and any X not defined over Q̄; (b) semiabelian varieties with nontrivial torus part (algebraic tori, general semiabelian varieties); (c) mixed Shimura varieties other than A₂ (Kuga type, other pure Shimura varieties); (d) for abelian varieties, finiteness of all atypical subvarieties rather than only the maximal ones; (e) subvarieties of A₂ of dimension ≥ 2; (f) effective or uniform bounds, none of which are claimed (the orbit and finiteness constants are ineffective).
entries.direction: proves a case: abelian varieties over Q̄ (maximal-atypical form), and curves in A₂ over Q̄ (Hodge-generic and special-closure)
entries.conditional_on: (1) Abelian paper: no unproven hypothesis is assumed; it relies on published results only (Barroero–Dill 2021 Thm 1.9, Habegger–Pila 2016 Thm 9.8, Ax's analytic-subgroup theorem and others) and on no other family manuscript. (2) E×CM: relies on Daw–Orr's implication (their Thm 1.2, taken from the corrected arXiv v4 rather than the published 2021 text, with the reduction-theory correction of Orr–Schnell), on Siegel's class-number bound (ineffective), and on Andre–Oort for A₂ (Pila–Tsimerman). Its effective-constant remark (rem:effective-cm) uses another OpenAI manuscript, the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis zero-free half-plane preprint (OAI:The-Quasi-Riemann-Hypothesis-September-30-2026). That manuscript is not in this family and I did not read it; the main theorems do not use the remark. (3) Quaternionic paper: no unproven hypothesis that I could identify; relies on Habegger–Pila Cor. 7.2 (quoted with k=1), Pila–Wilkie and Pila's counting results, Andre's monodromy theorem, and its own interpolation theorem (§2; I read only the statement). (4) Elliptic-squares paper: the E² theorem rests on Daw–Orr Thm 1.3 with their Conjecture 6.2, which the paper verifies for the E² locus only; it also uses Masser–Wüstholz endomorphism estimates and Andre's normality theorem. The full curve theorem (Thm intro:zp) and its special-closure corollary depend on two other family manuscripts: 'The E×CM component of Zilber–Pink for curves in A₂' (its Thm 1.1, which is item (2) here) and 'Quaternionic division points on curves in the Siegel threefold' (its Thm 1.1, which is item (3) here).
entries.doubts: (a) The abelian abstract calls its Q̄-restricted maximal-atypical statement 'the abelian Zilber–Pink conjecture'. The restriction to number fields appears in the theorem statement but not in the abstract's second sentence. (b) I did not check the proof of the auxiliary sequence theorem (§§2–8) line by line; the sections I read show no hedges. (c) E×CM: the Daw–Orr input is cited to the corrected arXiv v4 (2021), not the published text, and the footnote attributes the reduction-theory correction to Orr–Schnell. (d) E×CM: some steps are argued by citation rather than computed. The chart computation in Lemma boundary-comparison ends by invoking 'the fixed rational factor' and 'the fixed level datum'. Lemma family-height says an omitted finite set 'can be included by enlarging the constant'. (e) E×CM: the effective remark rests on a zero-free half-plane Re s > 7/8 for Dirichlet L-functions, cited to another OpenAI preprint. That is a very strong input, but the main theorems do not use it. (f) Quaternionic: the counting step (Prop counting-finiteness) is compressed. It says the arc has Nash coordinates 'algebraic over its real parameter' with 'transcendence degree at most one', and the quoted Habegger–Pila corollary is not restated in the section. (g) Elliptic squares: the interpolation theorem is titled 'Conditional height bound'. Its hypothesis (iv) is discharged in §07 (Prop nid:nonidentity), so the E² result depends on §07 being correct. (h) Elliptic squares: the paper calls its use of Daw–Orr Thm 1.3 'the precise E² case of the published conditional finiteness theorem'. The hypotheses in §§6.5–6.6 of Daw–Orr are cited, not restated, so the match is not checked here.
